topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Exploiting Locality
explanation: The memory hierarchy is a multi-level storage structure designed to mitigate the latency disparity between the high-speed CPU and slower main memory (DRAM). Caching strategies exploit the principle of locality to store frequently accessed data in faster, smaller cache levels (L1, L2, L3) closer to the processor core. Temporal locality predicts future access to recently used data, while spatial locality predicts access to data physically near recently used addresses. Maximizing the cache hit rate through effective locality exploitation minimizes the average memory access time (AMAT), which is critical for sustaining high instruction throughput.
